html:
SMTO-LLM-0028 — The model service didn't accept SMTO's list of tools

GUID: 24f69b0e-167b-45a8-94e1-b40c7ca2936d
Slug: tool-schema-rejected
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: provider

What happened

  • SMTO tells the model which actions it may take. The model service refused that list, so the model never answered and no action ran for this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Model routing, open the Main card, and select Check saved model. This sends one small test request with a single tool, showing whether your model service accepts tools at all.
  2. Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who runs your model service. Ask them to check the service's tool-calling support and settings. The details include the model name and the refusal code, which point them to the part of the request the service rejected.
  3. If they can't fix it soon, pick a different model in the Main card that supports tool calling, select Save Main, and start a new task. SMTO uses tool calling for every action it takes, so a model service that refuses tools can't run tasks.

What success looks like

  • Check saved model reports passed, and a new task gets past its first step without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages your model service or SMTO. Don't turn off SMTO's safety or security checks to get around this; the model service itself has to accept the request.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The model provider rejected the request (HTTP 400/422) and its error text matched tool-schema markers (schema, additionalProperties, tool_choice, tools.), so it was classified as tool_schema_rejected; this keyword match narrows the cause but is not a confirmed root cause.

What this means

  • The rejection classifier found wording associated with the tool schema. This narrows the next check but does not prove the provider’s exact internal failure. Check the recorded status and serving configuration before changing the request or installing components.

Why this can happen

  • Provider diagnostic text matched the tool schema category. The exact rejected feature still needs confirmation.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the provider’s supported tool schema and tool-choice features with the advertised request.
  • Have the provider operator reproduce the specific rejection with a small sanitized test, without sharing the original prompt or tool arguments.

How to fix it

  • Read http_status in the error details and the provider's server log for the same request, then compare the tool definitions and tool_choice SMTO sends with what the serving stack supports (for vLLM, the tool-call parser and JSON-schema features; for hosted APIs, their tool-schema rules). Fix the confirmed incompatibility on the provider side, or route the role in Settings › Setup › Model routing to a model and endpoint that support native tool calling, before starting another task.
  • Compare the provider’s supported tool schema and tool-choice features with the advertised request. Ask the provider operator to correct the confirmed incompatibility before another Agent decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The provider accepts a controlled request using the required native tool format.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • The category is selected by bounded provider-text markers, not authoritative structured root-cause evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
